Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 24-Dec-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  Natural Language Processing [NPT_4127]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                     Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Analyse the implications of skipping the 'Text Normalization' stage. How would this impact model        (4)  
  training efficiency, model accuracy, and error patterns during testing?  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Using the rule shown (noun + -ly → adjective), apply the morphological transformation to the            (4)  
  following nouns: love, cost, month. Write the resulting words and explain the meaning shift  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Apply syntactic analysis to the sentence 'The teacher discussed the problem with the student' by        (2)  
  showing two possible parse structures and explain how each structure gives a different meaning.  
  (Assume the proper rules)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                Evaluate the effectiveness of using the Minimum Edit Distance algorithm to convert the misspelled (4)  
  word 'recieve' into the correct form 'receive' when the operation costs are insert = 3, delete = 3, and  
  $$A)           substitute = 5.$$  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  B)           A system designer proposes the regular expression ^(0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01])/(0[1-9]|1[0-2])/[0-9]{2}\$ (4)  
  to validate dates in the format dd/mm/yy. Evaluate the adequacy of this regular expression. Does it  
  correctly capture all valid dates, and what limitations or edge cases reduce its reliability in real-world  
  applications.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  C)           Explain how stems and affixes differ in their roles within word formation, and describe how each        (2)  
  contributes to the overall meaning of a word with an example  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
3)                Evaluate the effectiveness of the Viterbi Algorithm by drawing the trellis diagram and predicting the   (4)  
  most likely sequence of Part-of-Speech (POS) tags for the sentence:  
  A)           "The dog chased the cat"  
  Given the following parameters:  
  States (Tags): Noun (N), Verb (V), Determiner (D)  
  Transition Probabilities:  
  
  Page #1

Emission probabilities  
  
  
  Initial Probabilities:  
  $$P(N) = 0.4, P(V) = 0.3, P(D) = 0.3$$  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  B)                                                                                                        (4)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)   Explain the bi-gram model with formulas.                                                             (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)        "The duck swims in the pond." vs. "I will duck under the table."                                     (4)  
  Analyse how morphological, syntactic, and contextual knowledge help a POS tagger correctly tag  
  A)   the word "duck" in each sentence and which type of knowledge plays the most significant role in  
  resolving such ambiguities.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)   For the given sentences:                                                                             (4)  
  • Birds can fly in the sky  
  • Sky is blue during the day  
  • Day turns into night  
  • Night is dark and quiet  
  Evaluate a bi-gram model using this data. Show the probabilities of all the words and estimate the  
  probability for the sentence "Birds can fly in the sky is blue during the day".  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  C)   Explain three methods of POS tagging.                                                                (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  
  Page #2

5)                       A chatbot is designed using hand-crafted grammar.                                              (4)  
  User: "I want to visit Paris."  
  A)               Bot: "When do you want to visit Paris?"  
  User: "Next week."  
  Bot (fails): "Next week what?"  
  Evaluate why hand-crafted grammar rules fail to interpret elliptical replies like "Next week,"  
  and argue whether a rule-based system could ever fully handle such dialogue ellipsis in real-  
  world contexts.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  B)               Consider the following CNF grammar:                                                                 (4)  
  S → NP VP  
  NP → Det N  
  NP → NP PP  
  VP → V NP  
  VP → VP PP  
  PP → P NP  
  Det → "the" | "a"  
  N → "student" | "professor" | "binoculars"  
  V → "watched"  
  P → "with" | "near"  
  Examine the CKY parse table for the sentence 'The professor watched the student with binoculars'  
  and identify the cell where PP-attachment ambiguity arises.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)               Explain the difference between dependency grammar and constituency grammar and how each             (2)  
  framework models sentence structure differently.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  
  -----End-----
